description: Grade 3 Phonics Unit: 5 phonetic skills + 2 decoding skills, large-font layout

blocks.text:
Vowel Teams

PHONICS SKILL 1 · LONG VOWEL PATTERNS

Rule: When two vowels are side by side, the first vowel usually says its own name (long sound). The second vowel is often silent.

  • ai / ay — rain, day
  • ee / ea — tree, read
  • oa / ow — boat, snow

Trick: ay and ow usually go at the end of a word. ai and oa usually go in the middle.

cells.text: rain · train · paint · day · play · stay
tree · sleep · green · read · team · clean
boat · coat · road · snow · grow · window

blocks.text:
Vowel Team Practice

PHONICS SKILL 1 · APPLY IT

Directions: Read each word aloud. Circle the vowel team you see.

1. rain    2. tree    3. boat    4. play    5. read    6. snow

7. train    8. clean    9. stay    10. grow

Sort it: Write each word from above under the correct heading: ai/ay, ee/ea, or oa/ow.

Challenge sentence: Decode this sentence, then underline every vowel team: "The team will stay and play in the rain until the boat is clean."

R-Controlled Vowels

PHONICS SKILL 2 · BOSSY R

Rule: When a vowel is followed by the letter r, the r "bosses" the vowel. It is no longer short or long — it makes its own special sound.

  • ar — car, farm
  • er / ir / ur — her, bird, hurt (all sound alike!)
  • or — corn, storm

Say it out loud: er, ir, and ur all make the same "er" sound — only the spelling changes.

cells.text: her · bird · hurt · first · turn · sister

blocks.text:
R-Controlled Practice

PHONICS SKILL 2 · APPLY IT

Directions: Read each word aloud. Underline the r-controlled vowel pattern.

1. car    2. bird    3. corn    4. her    5. storm    6. turn

7. shark    8. first    9. short    10. farm

Sort it: Write each word above under ar, er/ir/ur, or or.

Challenge sentence: Decode, then circle every r-controlled vowel: "The bird turned first, then the shark swam near the storm by the farm."

Diphthongs

PHONICS SKILL 3 · GLIDING VOWEL SOUNDS

Rule: A diphthong is two vowels that glide together to make one new sound — your mouth actually moves while you say it.

  • oi / oy — coin, toy
  • ou / ow — cloud, cow
  • au / aw — haul, paw

Trick: oy and aw usually go at the end of a word. oi and au usually go in the middle.

cells.text: coin · point · join · toy · boy · enjoy
cloud · sound · house · cow · town · crown
haul · August · sauce · paw · draw · lawn

blocks.text:
Diphthong Practice

PHONICS SKILL 3 · APPLY IT

Directions: Read each word aloud. Underline the diphthong.

1. coin    2. cloud    3. paw    4. toy    5. house    6. sauce

7. join    8. town    9. draw    10. enjoy

Sort it: Write each word above under oi/oy, ou/ow, or au/aw.

Challenge sentence: Decode, then circle every diphthong: "The boy saw a cloud shaped like a coin above the town."

Silent Letters

PHONICS SKILL 4 · TRICKY CONSONANTS

Rule: Some consonant pairs have a silent letter. You still write both letters, but you only hear one sound.

  • kn (silent k) — knee, know
  • wr (silent w) — write, wrist
  • mb (silent b) — comb, thumb
  • gh (silent gh) — light, night

These words are exceptions to the rules — readers just have to remember them.

cells.text: comb · thumb · climb · light · night · high

blocks.text:
Silent Letter Practice

PHONICS SKILL 4 · APPLY IT

Directions: Read each word aloud. Cross out the silent letter.

1. knee    2. write    3. comb    4. night    5. know    6. thumb

7. wrist    8. climb    9. knock    10. light

Sort it: Write each word above under kn, wr, or mb/gh.

Challenge sentence: Decode, then cross out every silent letter: "I know I should write my name before I climb into bed tonight."

Prefixes & Suffixes

PHONICS SKILL 5 · WORD PARTS

Rule: A prefix is added to the front of a word. A suffix is added to the end. Both change the word's meaning — and adding them creates a longer word to decode.

  • Prefixes: un- (not), re- (again), dis- (opposite)
  • Suffixes: -ing, -ed, -ly, -ful, -tion

Decoding tip: cover the prefix and suffix, read the root word first, then add the parts back on.

Prefix/Suffix Practice

PHONICS SKILL 5 · APPLY IT

Directions: Break each word into prefix/root/suffix, then read it aloud.

1. unhappy    2. rewrite    3. jumping    4. careful    5. disagree

6. quickly    7. painted    8. action    9. unlock    10. hopeful

Break it down: For each word above, write it like this: un + happy = unhappy.

Challenge sentence: Decode, then box every prefix and underline every suffix: "She carefully rewrote the unfinished story and quickly replayed the ending."

Syllable Division

DECODING SKILL 1 · BREAK IT DOWN

Rule: Long words are easier to read when you break them into syllables — small chunks with one vowel sound each.

  • Closed syllable — ends in a consonant, short vowel sound: rab·bit
  • Open syllable — ends in a vowel, long vowel sound: ti·ger
  • VC/CV pattern — two consonants in the middle, split between them: nap·kin

Decoding tip: find the vowels first, then decide where to split between them.

Syllable Division Practice

DECODING SKILL 1 · APPLY IT

Directions: Draw a line between the syllables in each word, then read it aloud.

1. rabbit    2. tiger    3. napkin    4. music    5. winter

6. picnic    7. paper    8. magnet    9. robot    10. supper

Label it: For each word above, write whether it is closed, open, or VC/CV.

Challenge sentence: Decode, splitting each long word into syllables first: "The tiger and rabbit shared a napkin at the winter picnic."

lessons.title: Structural Analysis
lessons.subtitle: Decoding multisyllabic words by word parts

blocks.text:
Structural Analysis

DECODING SKILL 2 · WORD DETECTIVE

Rule: Long, unfamiliar words are often built from smaller, known parts: prefix + root + suffix. Find the parts you know to decode the whole word.

  • Find the root word first — the main meaning.
  • Peel off any prefix at the start.
  • Peel off any suffix at the end.

Example: un·happi·ly = un (not) + happy + ly (in a way) — "not in a happy way."

Structural Analysis Practice

DECODING SKILL 2 · APPLY IT

Directions: Break each word into prefix / root / suffix, then read it aloud.

1. unfinished    2. replaying    3. disrespectful    4. careless

5. reappearance    6. unbelievable    7. disorganized    8. thoughtfully

Break it down: For each word above, write it like this: un + finish + ed = unfinished.

Challenge sentence: Decode, breaking each long word into parts first: "It was unbelievable how thoughtfully she reorganized the disorganized closet."
